name: Archaeological Site of Atapuerca
description: In the hills of Burgos province in northern Spain, the caves of Sierra de Atapuerca hold fossils of some of Europe's earliest humans, spanning nearly a million years. Bone fragments about 800,000 years old from the Gran Dolina cavern are the oldest evidence of human settlement in Western Europe. They also bear the world's oldest known signs of cannibalism among early humans.
